<note>This passage continues the story of the four brothers Cheng, Xiao, Renyi, and Youyu.</note>

They all contributed fields and houses for Cheng to live in. The elder brothers were angry at Xiao for being charitable. They went to his home to humiliate and distress him. Having spent a long time among the bandits, Cheng was accustomed to fierce and violent behavior. Hearing of this, he said in a great rage: "I have returned, and no one was willing to provide even a single room for me. Fortunately, my third brother remembered our kinship, yet you punish and blame him for it. Is it your intention to drive me away?"

He threw a stone at Xiao <note>The eldest brother</note>, who fell prostrate. Renyi and Youyu <note>The younger brothers</note> each came out with staffs to seize Zhong and Xin <note>The servants or younger kinsmen acting on the elders' behalf</note>, and flogged them countless times. Cheng did not wait for them to file a lawsuit; he sued them first before the District Magistrate. The Magistrate sent someone to invite Youyu for consultation. Youyu was forced to visit the Magistrate; he lowered his head and did not speak, only weeping. When the Magistrate pressed him with questions, he only begged the official to conduct the trial.

The Magistrate then ruled that Xiao and the others must each give up a portion of their fields and property to return to Cheng, making it so that the seven portions of the inheritance were equal. From this time on, Renyi and Cheng became increasingly loving and respectful toward one another. During a conversation, the subject of their mother's burial suddenly arose, and they both wept. Cheng said indignantly: "Such lack of benevolence <note>referring to the poor burial conditions</note> is the behavior of birds and beasts!"

He then wished to open the tomb to rebury her. Renyi ran to tell Youyu. Youyu hurried back to advise against it and stop him, but Cheng would not listen and set a date.

<summary>Cheng violently defends his brother Xiao against their elder brothers and wins a legal settlement for his inheritance. Tensions remain as Cheng insists on exhuming their mother for a proper burial against Youyu's advice.</summary>
<keywords>Pu Songling, Liaozhai Zhiyi, family conflict, inheritance law, filial piety, reburial, legal judgment</keywords>
